name: IDFA Bertha Fund — Classic
region: Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Caribbean & Oceania
description: Supports independent, author-driven documentary projects from countries where access to documentary funding and distribution is structurally limited.
eligibility: The director must be from, and currently live and work in, a country on the IBF Classic Country List. Development applications are director-led; production and post-production applications may be entered by a director or producer.
known_for: International support for filmmakers in underfunded regions

name: IDFA Bertha Fund — Europe
description: Minority co-production funding for creative documentaries made between an eligible European producer and a producer from an IBF-supported country.
eligibility: The application must come from an eligible European minority co-producer working with a producer from an IBF-supported country. For the January 2027 round, projects must be in edit stage and ideally have a rough cut.
known_for: International documentary co-production support

name: Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
description: Nonrecoupable support for independent, feature-length cinematic documentaries with strong artistic vision, cultural relevance, and meaningful filmmaker connection to the work.
eligibility: Independent feature documentaries of 52 minutes or longer are eligible worldwide. Sundance prioritizes budgets under $1.2 million and does not fund projects at picture lock.
known_for: One of documentary film's most significant global funds

name: SFFILM Documentary Film Fund
description: Supports feature documentaries approaching post-production that pair compelling subjects with an original and innovative visual approach.
eligibility: Open internationally to filmmakers age 18 or older in a key creative role. Projects must be feature documentaries and within roughly three months of beginning post-production by the final deadline.
known_for: Visually innovative documentaries nearing post-production

name: Catapult Development Grant
description: Early-stage funding for independent documentary features and shorts, designed to help filmmakers create a strong fundraising piece and unlock later production support.
eligibility: Independent documentary features and shorts in development may apply. Applicants should have a strong story, secured access, and a plan to produce a fundraising piece; docuseries are not supported.
known_for: Early money for documentary development

name: Frameline Completion Fund
description: Completion support for documentary, narrative, experimental, animated, and episodic projects that reflect LGBTQ+ lives and communities.
eligibility: Open internationally to projects about LGBTQ+ people and communities. Applicants must have creative and financial control, a full working cut, and at least 90% of production completed.
known_for: Completion funding for LGBTQ+ film and media

name: New York City Film Production Grant
description: Production funding for early-career New York City film directors whose work takes creative risks and expands, questions, or reimagines filmmaking.
eligibility: For eligible early-career directors who have lived in New York City for at least one year at the time of application. Step 2 is invitation-only after review of the initial application.
known_for: Risk-taking work by early-career NYC directors

name: Creative Capital Award
description: Unrestricted project grants and long-term professional support for bold, original work, including documentary, narrative, experimental film, and moving-image art.
eligibility: Lead applicants must be at least 25, have five years of professional artistic practice, and be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, Tribal ID holder, or O-1 visa holder. Current degree students and prior Creative Capital Awardees are ineligible.
known_for: Ambitious, formally inventive work across disciplines

name: IDA Emergency Assistance
description: Rapid-response support for independent documentary filmmakers facing government or politically motivated threats because of their film work.
eligibility: For independent documentary filmmakers whose safety, liberty, or ability to continue their work is under immediate threat as a direct consequence of their film work.
known_for: Confidential, rapid support for filmmakers in danger

name: Film Independent Camera Grant
description: A rolling in-kind grant of a professional digital camera body for an eligible independent narrative, documentary, short, feature, or web-series production.
eligibility: Applicants must be qualifying Film Independent or LA Film Festival alumni, past Spirit Award nominees, or invited filmmakers. The project must be at least 75% financed and apply at least 30 days before production.
known_for: Professional camera support for Film Independent alumni

name: ITVS Open Call
description: Co-production funding and editorial support for nonfiction documentaries in production or post-production that are intended for U.S. public media audiences.
eligibility: Independent producers of single nonfiction projects between 10 and 90 minutes may apply. ITVS funding is a co-production agreement with broadcast and streaming rights, not a grant.
known_for: Major public-media co-production support

name: NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowship — Video/Film
organization: New York Foundation for the Arts
description: An unrestricted award for New York State artists. Video/Film and Interdisciplinary Work are eligible disciplines in the 2027 cycle.
eligibility: Applicants must be at least 25 and have lived in New York State or a Tribal Nation located in New York State for the two consecutive years before the application deadline. This is an artist award, not a project grant.
known_for: Unrestricted support for New York artists

name: Manhattan Arts Grants — Creative Engagement
description: Project funding for Manhattan-based artists, collectives, and nonprofit organizations creating arts experiences for the public in Manhattan.
eligibility: Open across arts disciplines to eligible Manhattan-based individual artists, collectives, and nonprofit organizations. Proposed work must include a public-facing project in Manhattan; review the program track rules before applying.
known_for: Public arts projects across Manhattan

name: Queens Arts Fund — New Work Grant
organization: New York Foundation for the Arts
description: Supports Queens-based emerging artists and unincorporated collectives creating work that has not previously been produced or presented.
eligibility: Artists must live in Queens or hold a full-time studio lease there. The 2027 work must include an accessible public component for Queens audiences. Full-time degree students and 2026 New Work recipients are ineligible.
known_for: New work with a public component in Queens

name: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants
organization: New York Foundation for the Arts
description: Emergency support for artists in video/film, digital and electronic arts, visual arts, or choreography facing recent medical, dental, or mental-health expenses.
eligibility: For generative artists age 21 or older with at least five years of sustained public-facing practice, an eligible recent emergency, financial need under the program income ceiling, and treatment occurring in the United States.
known_for: Emergency medical support for working artists

name: NEA Grants for Arts Projects — Visual & Media Arts
description: Federal project funding for nonprofit arts organizations presenting, producing, commissioning, or supporting visual and media arts across the United States.
eligibility: Eligible applicants are U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state or local governments, and federally recognized Tribal communities with at least five years of arts programming and the required operating history. Individuals and fiscal sponsors cannot apply; a 1:1 cost share is required.
known_for: National public funding for visual and media arts

name: USA Fellowship
description: A major unrestricted fellowship for artists and collaboratives across film, media, visual art, writing, performance, design, craft, music, and traditional arts.
eligibility: Artists do not apply through an open call. A rotating network of arts professionals anonymously nominates artists and collaboratives from across the United States and its jurisdictions for panel review.
known_for: One of the largest unrestricted U.S. artist awards

name: (Egg)celerator Lab
region: Worldwide, subject to U.S. sanctions restrictions
description: A two-year documentary lab pairing a production grant with creative mentorship, industry meetings, and peer support for first- and second-time feature documentary directors.
eligibility: Open to women (cis or trans) and gender-expansive directors working on a first or second feature-length documentary of at least 48 minutes. Directors may be based worldwide except where U.S. sanctions prevent funding; projects must be in production.
known_for: Career-building support for women and gender-expansive documentary directors

name: Alter-Ciné Documentary Film Grants
description: Annual production grants for independent documentary filmmakers whose work explores the realities of communities and social change across the Global South.
eligibility: Applicants must have been born in and currently live in a country in Africa, Asia, or Latin America. The fund supports feature-length documentary projects in production and does not fund fiction.
known_for: Long-running documentary support for Global South filmmakers

name: William Greaves Research & Development Fund
region: North, Central & South America and the Caribbean
description: Unrestricted research and development support for established nonfiction storytellers pursuing ambitious film or video-art projects at an early stage.
eligibility: For established filmmakers and media artists of African and/or Indigenous descent who live and work in the Americas or Caribbean. Candidates are nominated; the fund does not accept unsolicited applications.
known_for: Early-stage support for Black and Indigenous nonfiction auteurs

name: AXS Film Fund
region: No residency restriction listed in the published criteria
description: Supports feature documentaries and nonfiction new-media projects, with a mission centered on creators living with disabilities and historically underserved communities.
eligibility: Applicants must be at least 18, cannot be enrolled in a degree program, and must be the director or producer. Feature documentaries of 45+ minutes and nonfiction new media are eligible at any stage. Disabled creators are prioritized, although the published criteria welcome all applicants; confirm current residency rules with the fund.
known_for: Accessible support for disabled and underrepresented nonfiction creators

name: Building Bridges Documentary Fund
description: Development, production, and post-production funding for feature documentaries that tell nuanced stories about Muslim communities and the U.S. Muslim experience.
eligibility: For independent feature documentary projects about the U.S. Muslim experience. Applicants do not need to identify as Muslim. Award size varies by stage; review the current call for complete applicant and public-media requirements.
known_for: Substantial documentary funding for complex U.S. Muslim stories

name: Creative Shorts Fellowship
description: A mentored short-film fellowship supporting emerging Native filmmakers and inventive Indigenous stories across documentary, experimental, animation, and narrative forms.
eligibility: For emerging Native filmmakers developing a short project. Current calls define eligible tribal affiliation, team roles, format, length, and delivery requirements; consult the official guidelines before applying.
known_for: Native-led public-media storytelling and filmmaker development

name: Fellowships and Grants
region: Asia ↔ United States and intra-Asia exchange
description: Fellowships and organizational grants supporting immersive cultural exchange for artists, scholars, and arts professionals traveling between Asia and the United States or within Asia.
eligibility: Programs include individual, New York, graduate, and organization awards. Applicants must propose an eligible cultural-exchange experience involving the United States and Asia or travel within Asia; rules and support vary by program type.
known_for: Established international arts exchange fellowships since 1963

name: Anonymous Was A Woman Environmental Art Grants
organization: New York Foundation for the Arts
description: Project grants for environmental art led by women, transgender, and gender-nonconforming artists working across visual, media, performance, and interdisciplinary practices.
eligibility: Lead artists must identify as women, transgender, or gender-nonconforming and live in the United States or a U.S. territory. Projects must engage environmental issues and meet the current cycle's public-presentation and timeline requirements.
known_for: Environmental art support for women and gender-expansive artists
